to modify zoning and transportation regulations, to create new zoning districts
and establish regulations, and to enhance and streamline street design,
building, and site development standards to enhance multimodal mobility
throughout the City and report back to Council. 

Transportation-related recommendations: (A) As part of the upcoming update to
the TCM to integrate green infrastructure rules as part of sidewalk corridor
design requirements and provide a comprehensive update of streetscape design
requirements for all street types, with a particular focus on pedestrian realm
design requirements; and (B) Consolidate and co-locate right-of-way design
requirements into the TCM; and (C) Develop proposed City Code amendments to
simplify and consolidate streetscape requirements in the Land Development Code
that reference the TCM for specifications and detailed implementation rules and
to eliminate conflicting and duplicative administrative criteria, consolidating
and coordinating right-of-way design requirements in the TCM; and (D) Develop
and apply clear street design standards based on ASMP street tiers, reflecting
each tier’s intended prioritization of pedestrian or automobile orientation, as
well as proximity to transit station areas, and along high-frequency transit
lines; and (E) (F) Update pedestrian realm design standards to work cohesively
with the street’s modal needs as identified in the ASMP and adopted modal and
transit plans to prioritize, coordinate, and allocate space within
rights-of-way; and Update streetscape requirements to maximize connectivity and
walkability to transit stops, activity centers, neighborhood centers, and any
other area of growth or vibrancy; and (G) Ensure that new pedestrian realm
requirements reflect desired outcomes for the upcoming Central City planning
area and future Downtown Density Bonus programs, and consider streetscape design
typologies as needed to supplement baseline citywide standards; and (H) Provide
a plan and timeline for Council to consider updates to all approved regulating
plans to comply with streetscape standards in the Land Development Code; and
(I) Integrate the Project Connect Design Guidelines into the updated TCM as
baseline streetscape requirements for relevant transit corridors; and (J)
Integrate the Project Connect Design Guidelines into the updated TCM as baseline
streetscape requirements for relevant transit corridors; and Identify
opportunities to streamline the process for review and approval of site
development standards and design requirements based on right-of-way designation,
particularly for residential review; and (K) Clarify decision-making or
escalation pathways when there are conflicts; and (L) Explore and recommend
strategies to require mid-block bike/pedestrian crossing improvements in
conjunction with new development in locations where crossing gaps or uses
identified as pedestrian generators exist.
